intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fantastic 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the porter wrote of ① a fantastic view from the top in the journal, and everybody in the coast said at once that it was ② more fantastic than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the porter, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the fantastic ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most fantastic view from the top anybody in the coast had ever seen, or so the journal for August 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fantastic to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the fantastic ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fantastic tale about the lake, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fantastic as the tale about the lake they had once had in the old coast. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fantastic or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fantastic, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next coast called the whole plan ⑧ quite fantastic; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the fantastic ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, before dawn, she wrote of another fantastic view from the top in the same journal, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more fantastic than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most fantastic tale about the lake in the whole coast, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the fantastic ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 极好（前置定语 a fantastic view from the top：1981 年挑夫在行记里记下的那件极好的景致）
B. adj. 极好／奇异（比较级 more fantastic than：文中两处，一处比顶上看到的景致，一处比预想）
C. adj. 极好／奇异（最高级 the most fantastic：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 极好（表语 too fantastic to do：母亲觉得它太极好，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 奇异（前置定语 a fantastic tale about the lake：叔叔把整件事称作一桩奇异的传说）
F. adj. 奇异（同级比较 as fantastic as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩关于那个湖的奇异传说相比）
G. adj. 奇异（后置定语 something fantastic：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 奇异（受程度副词修饰 quite fantastic：那位游客的评价）

answers.why: fantastic 意为“极好”，1981 年挑夫在行记里记下的是“一件极好的景致”，此处作前置定语 a fantastic view from the top。
fantastic 意为“极好”，此处用比较级 more fantastic than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fantastic 意为“极好”，行记上 八月 那行字说它是海岸里最极好的一件，故用最高级 the most fantastic view from the top。
fantastic 意为“极好”，母亲认为这件东西“太极好了，谁也用不上”，too fantastic to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩奇异的传说”，此处作前置定语 a fantastic tale about the lake。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩关于那个湖的奇异传说一样奇异”，同级比较用 as fantastic as。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，行记上那半行字要的是“奇异的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fantastic。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，邻海岸来的那位游客认为这套计划“相当奇异”，quite 修饰原级 fantastic。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，1991 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要奇异”，故用比较级 more fantastic than。
fantastic 意为“奇异”，母亲 1993 年说的是“整个海岸里最奇异的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most fantastic tale about the lake。
